I've verified every document in the corpus whose text contains "disparag*" (10 documents), plus alternate phrasings ("derogatory", "defame", "speak ill", "negative statement", "nondisparagement"), which surfaced no additional documents. Here is the breakdown.

## Contracts with a genuine non-disparagement clause (a party covenants not to disparage the other)

| # | Contract | doc_id | Clause |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | **Papa John's International – Endorsement Agreement** (8-K, 6/17/2019; with Shaquille O'Neal/ABG) | `a30ad65d-2370-4336-87f9-0f8823e8e096` | **§10 "Confidentiality and Non-Disparagement"** (p. 24): "All Parties agree not to disparage or make derogatory comments, verbal or written, regarding the other Party during the Term of the Agreement, and for one year thereafter." Also **§5 "Brand Restrictions"** (pp. 5-6): Papa John's shall not, during the Term or at any time thereafter, "defame or disparage CELEBRITY or the Personality Rights… nor… place the CELEBRITY… in a negative light." (The word also appears at p. 18 in a termination trigger for conduct "egregiously disparaging or insulting any group of the community.") |
| 2 | **Pelican Delivers – Development Agreement 2** (S-1, 2/11/2020; with Seattle Software Developers) | `5db63bc4-f1f1-4073-8b82-332ae253c31c` | **§10.3 "NON DISPARAGEMENT CLAUSE"** (pp. 9-10): Client and Designer "agree to never to disparage or speak ill of the other party to anyone and or post negative or disparaging comments Online…"; defines "disparage" as "any negative statement whether written or oral"; both agree not to post negative reviews on review websites; expressly a "material term of this Agreement." |
| 3 | **STAAR Surgical – Distributor Agreement** (10-Q, 8/1/2018) | `7de22e9f-30e5-4d0f-b1a9-5345b4c39de0` | **§6.7** (p. 5): Distributor shall "refrain from making any claims or representations concerning the Products other than as set forth in the applicable specifications or labeling therefor and **never disparage either STAAR or the Products**." (One-way obligation on the Distributor.) |
| 4 | **Bizzingo – Celebrity Endorsement Agreement** (8-K, 3/22/2012; with Joe Theismann) | `d5cc977c-30a6-4b59-964b-c1f215a382ec` | **§19 "CONFIDENTIALITY AND NON-DISPARAGEMENT AGREEMENT"** (p. 7): "Concurrent with the execution of this agreement, the parties will execute a mutually acceptable Confidentiality and Non-Disparagement Agreement." Note: this is a covenant to sign a *separate* non-disparagement agreement; the substantive restriction itself is not in this document. |

## Borderline / related provisions (contain disparagement language but not a classic non-disparagement covenant)

| Contract | doc_id | What it actually says |
|---|---|---|
| **Cybergy Holdings – Affiliate Agreement** (10-Q, 5/20/2014) | `b7f37b40-c3d8-4630-b91e-9d3c862202c6` | "Business Practices" (p. 3): MA must avoid "deceptive, misleading or unethical practices that… might be detrimental to Company… **including but not limited to disparagement of Company or the Technology**." Functionally a non-disparagement obligation embedded in a business-conduct clause. |
| **Berkshire Hills Bancorp – Endorsement Agreement** (10-Q, 8/9/2012; with Geno Auriemma) | `43095b35-9378-4710-8e52-06ae5f8f292a` | Termination right (pp. 6-7): Berkshire may terminate if "Auriemma publicly disparages Berkshire and/or its products." A termination trigger, not a stand-alone covenant. |
| **Rand Worldwide – Co-Branding Agreement** (8-K/A, 4/2/2001) | `01344d95-68ef-4660-9286-a6308349bd1a` | Trademark license (p. 5): each party "agrees not to use the other party's Marks in any manner that is disparaging or that otherwise portrays such party in a negative light." Limited to use of marks. |
| **Creditcards.com – Chase Affiliate Agreement** (S-1, 8/10/2007) | `e63b7241-fb85-4319-9691-94ffa08a7054` | License clause (pp. 6-12): "Affiliate agrees not to use the Licensed Materials in any manner that is disparaging or that otherwise portrays Chase in a negative light." Limited to use of licensed materials. |
| **Digital Cinema Destinations – NCM Affiliate Agreement** (S-1, 12/20/2011) | `4be07132-7e4f-4b89-8ff6-4e48d0884e88` | Trademark license (p. 20): NCM may suspend/terminate the license if Affiliate's use of the NCM Marks "is otherwise disparaging to NCM's image or reputation." Remedy tied to mark usage. |

## Not a non-disparagement clause (word appears only incidentally)

- **eDiets.com – Women.com Co-Branding Agreement** (`3c40cba1-a4cc-47f4-a1a6-2011dc83888a`): §12.3(f) is a content warranty that publication "will not constitute defamation, **product disparagement** or trade libel" — a legal-claim warranty, not a non-disparagement covenant.

**Summary:** Four contracts have a true non-disparagement clause — **Papa John's (mutual, Term + 1 year)**, **Pelican Delivers (mutual, titled §10.3)**, **STAAR Surgical (one-way on Distributor, §6.7)**, and **Bizzingo (§19, obligating the parties to execute a separate Non-Disparagement Agreement)**. Cybergy's business-practices clause arguably qualifies as well; the remaining four are mark-usage restrictions or termination triggers rather than general non-disparagement covenants.
